scope: Independent source/API/control review of the isolated Android pylon targeting fixture. No Android compile or native execution.

initial_issue.detail: The first draft referenced protected PixelScene.Fader and private INSTANCE directly. The extracted Probe type check intentionally excluded that method. Static source review found the access violation before CI.
initial_issue.resolved: Uses the already established Class.forName/declared-field reflection pattern, retaining the first draft.

reviewed_behavior: Concrete mobs and real linked sprites, existing public Pylon.activate, actual Dungeon.observe and hero.checkVisibleMobs, actual AttackIndicator.target/updateState. No overridden targeting or damage handler.
Actual ranged, inventory and health targets are asserted independently from the melee indicator and portrait class.
Terrain walls establish hidden-target exclusion; the real FOV is read and recomputed rather than supplied as the expected value.
The same real current hero actor, world/hero clocks and all HP values are checked before and after capture; no input action or attack is performed.
Map setup clears discarded floor objects and marks the newly opened floor as discoverable. It is a disposable synthetic arena, not a natural boss-floor encounter.
Only an initially empty class save slot is used and later deleted. Title is requested even when fixture cleanup throws; RNG/settings/selection flags are restored.
limitations: Five selection states in one method; no full boss fight, actual touch dispatch, attack, projectile flight, damage, natural phase transition or physical-device result.
Existing six headless call-site regressions remain separate. The new native fixture does not cover the vulnerable-boss or visible-but-blocked/mind-vision controls.
Review validates the intended assertions and API access; the Android compiler and emulator must establish actual viability.
